title: Loops — typing drills
description: Type for, while, break, and continue. Spacing is flexible, and a trailing semicolon is fine.

drills.prompt: Write a for loop header that uses range(3) and a loop variable named i.
drills.hint: for, the name i, in, range(3), then a colon. range(3) gives 0, 1, and 2.
drills.explain: range(3) starts at 0 and stops before 3, so the body runs for 0, 1, and 2.

drills.prompt: Write a for loop header that walks each item in inventory, using a loop variable named item.
drills.hint: for item in inventory, then a colon. You do not need range here.
drills.explain: This walks the array in order. On each pass, item is the next value in inventory.

drills.prompt: Type the keyword that stops a loop right away.
drills.hint: It is one word. Once the monster finds a target, there is no need to keep scanning.
drills.explain: break leaves the loop immediately. The code after the loop is what runs next.

drills.prompt: Type the keyword that skips the rest of this pass and goes to the next item.
drills.hint: It is one word, and it does not stop the whole loop.
drills.explain: continue skips the rest of the current pass only. The loop keeps going with the next item.

drills.prompt: Write a while loop header that keeps running while fear is less than max_fear.
drills.hint: while, then the condition, then a colon. Make sure the body will eventually raise fear, or this could run forever.
drills.explain: A while loop keeps going as long as its condition is true, and it stops as soon as fear is no longer less than max_fear.
